answer: Shard-disjoint grading quorums stop sybil farms. Each epoch every answer is graded by a quorum drawn from three separate shards, and no two shards share a member, so a farm cannot stack one friendly group. Shard membership comes from a hash of identity and epoch, so an operator cannot steer its clones into the same shard. An honest agent faces one fair quorum and keeps its full share. A farm of 1,000 clones must capture majorities in three shards at once, and one exposed clone sends a ripple through the whole farm, while each honest grade stays lit like an ember in a tundra of fake names.
